verdict: Meta is working; Google's spend is not converting and is being addressed.
narrative: In the last 28 days, you received 28 leads at an average cost per lead of $148.60 — all of them came from Meta, which delivered those leads on $1,507.79 in spend, roughly $54 per lead. Google Ads consumed $2,652.98 in the same window and produced 2 conversions, a cost per lead of roughly $1,326; that gap is structural, not a slow week, and Google's budget allocation is being reviewed now. Separately, your pipeline shows 108 new opportunities logged this period but no appointments booked against them, which points to an intake process issue rather than an ads problem — that is being looked at in parallel. Next period you can expect tighter Google spend controls and a focused push on converting the leads already in your pipeline into booked consultations.

watch_item.issue: Google Ads is spending at roughly $1,326 per conversion this period — a structural inefficiency, not normal variance.
watch_item.fix: Google campaign budget and targeting are being restructured this week to stop inefficient spend while Meta carries lead volume.
